title: Escalating wrongly? Fix the boundary, not a proxy
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Guidance is vague, errors in both directions
Clear criteria and examples exist and still fail
Heavier, justified only after the cheap fix
rule: Self-rated confidence and sentiment don't measure complexity. When the escalation boundary is vague, write explicit criteria and show contrasting examples first.

title: When should the agent hand over to a person?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Customer explicitly asks for a person
Customer angry, issue simple and in scope
Acknowledge, offer the fix; escalate if they then ask again
Policy is silent or needs an exception
Escalation driven by sentiment or self-rated confidence
rule: Escalate on categories: an explicit request (at once), a policy gap, or no progress. Tone and self-rated confidence are not triggers.

title: Who is this customer? Pick the source of truth
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Chat arrives with a signed-in, verified account
Return all matches; ask for order number or postcode
Refund attempted before identity is verified
Ranking or confidence used to pick a match
Replace with a question to the customer
rule: Several matching records means ask the customer for an identifier. Do not choose by recency, score or ranking.

title: Escalation is miscalibrated: what is the proportionate fix?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Agent escalates easy cases and keeps going on hard ones
Explicit criteria + a few contrasting examples
Large labelled history, time to build and maintain
Routing by sentiment or self-rated confidence
Customer explicitly asks for a person
Human receiving an escalation lacks context
Improves the handoff, not the decision
rule: Fuzzy escalation boundaries get explicit triggers plus a few contrasting examples, not a new model.

title: Escalate or resolve? Ask which trigger is present
head: Situation
Agent should
Why
rows: Escalate immediately, with a handoff summary
Customer frustrated, hasn't asked; issue is simple
Policy is silent or needs an exception
rule: Explicit request for a person → escalate now, with the facts. Frustration alone → offer resolution first.
